story.soThat: we can design the G36 Service architecture correctly

Test state serialization - check if canGetAndSetFMUstate=true, attempt save/restore

constraints.constraint: All units in SI (Kelvin for temperature, m3/s for airflow)

API design must support both stateful and stateless patterns until POC determines which

inputs.real: TZon (K), TCooSet (K), THeaSet (K), TDis (K), VDis_flow (m3/s), TSup (K), TSupSet (K)

ideas.idea: Statefulness test: Run TZon=291K,THeaSet=293K for steps 1-10, observe if yVal increases (integral action)
Pure function test: Reset FMU, repeat step 1, verify same yVal as original step 1
API Pattern A: Single instance per zone (session-based) - step repeatedly
API Pattern B: Fresh instance per call (stateless) - instantiate/step/terminate each call
State persistence: Check modelDescription.xml for canGetAndSetFMUstate=true
Memory footprint: Measure memory before/after instantiation

questions.question: Does doStep(stepSize=300) mean "advance 5 minutes of simulated time"?
Is it real-time or simulated time?
Does FMU run continuously or wait for step calls?

expectedFindings.finding: FMUs are typically stateful - internal state evolves with simulation time
State save/restore may be supported via fmi2GetFMUstate/fmi2SetFMUstate
G36 controller likely has integral terms - NOT a pure function

ifStateful.recommendation: Session-based API with zone-specific FMU instances

ifStateless.recommendation: Simple REST API - instantiate/step/terminate per request
